text: The administration surface is one read of rwb-access that answers one row per capability area in force with the caller's letters, the role's default scope and mayOpen, and the surface itself is composed at the edge from that answer plus each owner's own panel list (queues and parameters of rwb-case, templates of rwb-comms, panels of rwb-partner, autonomy of rwb-agent); rwb-access holds no panel list and shows no panel the answer does not entitle.
why: The sources name one place for roles, queues, parameters, templates, panels and autonomy but give no operation for it, and five services own the panels, so the entitlement answer and the composition have to be placed somewhere before the story can be built.
read: RWB-E8-006 AC1 and its screen table; FSD P4 v3 A2.17.1 and A2.17.2; DP-19 and Architecture v5 slide 14 (P4 owns roles, scope, masking and DoA, not queues or templates); the ownership map for queue, template and partner_user.
confirm: Security administrator and the tech lead of the gateway-bff contract
impact: If the answer must also carry the panel list, this service would hold another service's data and the composite route would become a pass-through.

text: The cache lifetime of the entitlement answer is the parameter row access.home.cache.ttl.seconds of rwb-case, read through DP-06 with the version in force; the name is fixed by this story and its contract and the value is data, never a constant in code.
why: The answer is read on every open of the administration surface and the sources name no lifetime and no parameter that holds one, so a lifetime has to be decided and it must be changeable without a build.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.17.3.1 BR-P4-017 (no value a business person may change is written in code); DP-06 and the ownership ruling that parameters stay with rwb-case (ASM-A6-tables-5); TSD P4 v3 T3.2 for the style of the list and parameter names.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-case (P3) and the platform administrator
impact: A different row name or owner is a parameter-row change and a contract note within major version 1; no schema change.

text: The entry of an open of the administration surface carries the local decision-record library's read code, with the caller reference, the matrix version, the masking version and the areas answered, and no case id.
why: The legacy criterion requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version, and the library's codes are the library's to publish; the sources do not name the code of an entitlement read.
read: RWB-E8-006 AC1 and AC2; DP-03 (local decision-record library and rwb.decision-record.v1); FSD P4 v3 A2.7 and A2.17.4.3; the decision-code set already used for access events (AC-READ, AC-DENY, AC-EXPT).
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-decision (P7) as the owner of the ledger view and the library owner
impact: If the library publishes a distinct code for an entitlement read, only the entry code changes and the answer and its fields stay as the contract fixes them.

text: The rule-change request is a record of rwb-access and not a table of rwb-access: one entry of the local decision-record chain of the DP-03 library, written with an idempotency row in the same transaction, with the rule package version consumed through the P7 contract and its fake. The missing RWB-P7 rule-package contract dependency is raised at D1 and is not added to the metadata of this story.
why: The rule registry, its versions and its rows are P7's under ASM-A6-tables-3 and ASM-A6-api-3, so this service can neither hold the version nor read a rule table, while an administrative decision that is not recorded cannot be defended; the sources name no table and no operation for the change request itself.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 and T4; Temporal and Drools design slide 15 (governance central in rwb-decision); ownership map rows rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case and the rule-package API paths (ASM-A6-tables-3, ASM-A6-api-3); DP-01 and DP-03.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-decision and the tech lead of rwb-access
impact: A cross-service change record needs a registry table or a central record instead of the local chain, and the audit consumer would read P7 rather than rwb-access.

text: The seven items of TSD P4 v3 T6.3 — request, impact, test result, approver, load, verify and rollback plan — are the change checklist of the change request, checked for completeness when the change is raised and carried as the seven required item codes of the RuleChangeChecklist schema; a missing item is refused 422 with MSG-P3-022 naming the item code.
why: The technical specification attaches the checklist to the approval of a version and names no check at the point where the change is raised, and this story must refuse an incomplete change before any registry hop so the analyst learns the missing item while the change is still only a form.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (change_checklist, DF-REF-295, MSG-P3-022); FSD P4 v3 A2.18; the message table of the rule-change stories for the text of MSG-P3-022; the pattern list of the key holds no DP07 and the contract-dependency list no RWB-P3-E1043-CON, so the item codes are contract constants rather than a reference-data read.
confirm: Centre of excellence and the internal audit representative
impact: If the checklist belongs only to the approval, the change request carries the items as reference and the registry remains the only gate; the 422 of an incomplete change would then become a warning and no change would be refused here.

text: The record code of an administrative change is the administrative-change code of the local decision-record library, and the change entry is written under it with the change id in the reference field of the entry; the change id is minted by this service and is opaque to every consumer.
why: The sources fix the decision codes of a case decision and of an access event and give no code for an administrative change, and the entry must be findable by the identifier the screen and the audit quote.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (a change log entry is append only, with the version label, the status change, the author or approver and the time); LDM v8 DF-DEC-003 for the decision code and DF-DEC-008 for the reference field; DP-03 for the local library.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-access and the owner of the decision-record library
impact: A different record code changes the value written on every change entry and the filter the audit consumer uses; the entry would still be found by its change id.

text: A move writes a new delegation_limit row that carries the next limit_version of the same limit in state PENDING_APPROVAL, and the row in force is changed only at the approval, when it is closed with valid_to and state SUPERSEDED; the decision code, the level, the product group and the conditions of the moved row are copied from the row it moves, because this story's pattern list carries no DP-07 and its contract-dependency list no RWB-P3-E1043-CON.
why: The legacy story and the FSD name the move and no row model, and the table is a version-carrying table of this service, so the change has to be modelled either as an edit of the row in force or as a new row version; an edit would let a limit change before Risk approves it.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.19 and A2.6.4.2; TSD P4 v3 T3.0 (state, version), T3.1 delegation_limit DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026 and DF-REF-055 to DF-REF-062; Temporal and Drools design (versioned limits, approve-and-date); Architecture v5 slide 14; ownership map ASM-A6-tables-4.
confirm: Risk and model risk officer and the tech lead of RWB-P4-E1038-APP
impact: If a move must edit the row in force instead, the approval gate disappears and the lookup of RWB-P4-E2013-APP can answer a limit that Risk has not approved.

text: The row a move supersedes carries valid_to as the day before the valid_from of the row that supersedes it, and its state becomes SUPERSEDED in the same transaction as the approval, so exactly one version of a limit is in force on any date.
why: The sources fix that rows stay readable with a valid_to once a new version is approved and name no rule for the closing date of a move, so the day-before rule has to be chosen or two rows would be in force on the effective date.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.6.4.2 (the rows of DOA-2026.11 stay readable with valid_to 2026-12-31 while DOA-2027.01 is in force from 2027-01-01); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-025 and DF-REF-026; Temporal and Drools design.
confirm: Risk and model risk officer and the tech lead of rwb-access
impact: A different closing date leaves two rows in force on the day a change takes effect, and the lookup of RWB-P4-E2013-APP would answer the lower level or the higher one depending on the order of the rows.

text: The change event rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1 is published on rwb.access.events.v1, keyed by delegationLimitId, with the payload delegationLimitId, limitVersion, decisionCode, approvalLevel, productGroup, effectiveFrom and reason, and with no holder reference, no substitute reference and no personal data.
why: Architecture v5 names the event on the topic and names no payload, so the field list and the exclusion of the person references have to be fixed or the event would either be unusable by a subscriber or publish the delegation table's person references to every consumer.
read: Architecture v5 slide 14 and slide 41 (rwb.access.events.v1: AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-017 to DF-REF-019, DF-REF-023, DF-REF-024 and DF-REF-055; NFR-040; DP-09.
confirm: Risk and model risk officer and the data steward
impact: A payload that carries the holder or the substitute publishes person references to every subscriber; a payload without the version or the effective date cannot be used to refresh a limit cache.

text: The treatment policy edition travels as one workbook file that rwb-access passes unchanged to P3 rwb-case POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads with the table code product_policy and the valid-from date, so every band, floor and range stays with its owner and this service reads out of the file only the presence of its three parts and their row counts. The three parts are one sheet each for the bands, the floors and the ranges, each with a header row; the sheet names, the header rows, the accepted media types and the upload size cap are fixed at contract review with the owner. The state of a load is read through the owner's load read GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}, declared as consumed although the TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A does not list it, and the screen that carries the edition is served through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 because no source names it. The reference-load contract is called through its contract and its fake and is not added to the metadata dependency rows.
why: The parameters and reference data, the reference-load operations and the treatment entity belong to other services under the R-PREC default ruling and the ownership map, and no source gives the table code, the sheet names or a load read, so the transport and the parts have to be fixed as a default before the build; leaving them open would stop the story and inviting the values into rwb-access would create a second copy of a versioned table.
read: Template and Rules v1 section R3 default ruling and R5.5 DP-07; TSD P4 v3 T3.2, T4 and appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P4-004 to API-P4-010); FSD P4 v3 A2.20.2; Program BRD REQ-DRI-010; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (lov_value, reference_version, reference_row, treatment, POST /admin/reference-loads); legacy RWB-E8-009 story statement
applied_in: Section 1; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 5, 8 and 12; section 5 X3 and X8; section 7 AC4; section 8 BR1, BR3, BR6 and BR10; section 11 Data; section 12.1, 12.2, 12.7 and 12.8; section 13; section 15
confirm: Solution architect and the tech lead of rwb-case (P3) at the contract review of RWB-P4-E8009-CON, with the product head as the business reader
impact: A renamed table code, a different set of sheet names or an owner-side load read of another shape changes the controller, the client and the fake only, with no change to the rights, the messages or the record content; if the owner refuses to accept a pass-through file, the edition would have to be modelled as a value set and the ownership ruling would have to change first.

text: The product head proposes the edition and does not submit it. TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-PRODHEAD R only in Rules and parameters, RW-COE CRUD there and RW-RISK RA there, and the legacy permission table gives the C letter to RW-COE and the A letter to RW-RISK. R-PREC puts the Technical Specifications above the story master, and the FSD makes the product head the primary role of the feature, so the story reads the three sources together as: the product head opens the screen, prepares the edition and proposes it with R; a holder of the C letter, RW-COE, submits it through POST /admin/product-policies; and the A letter approves a load on the console reference-load path, which is RWB-P4-AD010-APP's and not this story's. A product head posting an edition is therefore refused 403 with MSG-P4-002, which is the refusal AC3 tests.
why: Three sources disagree on who may act: the FSD calls the product head primary, the TSD gives it R only, and the legacy table gives the C letter to RW-COE; a story that silently granted the product head the C letter would contradict the matrix and a story that removed the product head from the feature would contradict the FSD, so the reading has to be recorded before the build.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.20.3.3 and A2.20.4.1; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and the rule package and workflow refinement table; legacy RWB-E8-009 permission checks; Template and Rules v1 section R3 R-PREC order and §R5.5 DP-08 (the matrix is data); Program BRD REQ-ACA-003 and REQ-ACA-013
applied_in: Section 2; section 5 X5 and X11; section 7 AC3; section 8 BR4 and BR5; section 10 Authority; section 12.1; section 14; and in the contract story section 7 AC1, section 8 BR7, section 10 and section 12.1
confirm: Solution architect with the owner of the permission matrix and the product head as the business reader, at the contract review of RWB-P4-E8009-CON; a change is a permission row and not a code change
impact: If the matrix is later changed to give RW-PRODHEAD the C letter, AC3 changes to the opposite answer and only a permission row and that one test change; if the four-eyes reading is rejected, RW-COE submits and RW-RISK approves the load and this story's own operations are unaffected.

text: An accepted edition appends exactly one entry to the local decision-record chain of DP-03 carrying the editionId, the productGroup, the policyVersion label, the loadId the owner answered, the validFrom date, the version in force read from the parameters contract at the time and the caller reference, and nothing else: no band, no floor, no range, no amount, no percentage and no personal field. The record code that marks the entry as a treatment policy edition is not in any source, so the entry uses the DP-03 library's administrative-change code and the contract review fixes the value with the ledger owner. The entry, the idempotency row and the answer commit in one local transaction, and where the entry cannot be written the answer is withheld with 503 and MSG-P7-003, which is what legacy AC2 asserts as nothing changing.
why: Legacy AC1 requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version, and legacy AC2 requires nothing to change when the log cannot be written, but no source names the record code of an administrative change or says which version label the entry carries; the record has to be fixed as a default or neither criterion can be tested.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-009 AC1 and AC2, the message table and the data table (DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018); TSD P4 v3 T3.2, T4 and T6.3 (the change log entry of a load, an approval and a rollback is append only); FSD P4 v3 A2.20.4.1 and A2.20.4.3 (AC-EXC-P4-020-02); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-03; Program BRD REQ-DRI-010
applied_in: Section 4 Flow steps 10 and 11; section 5 X9; section 7 AC2 and AC5; section 8 BR8 and BR9; section 11 Data; section 12.3 and 12.7; section 13 Database and migrations; and in the contract story section 11, section 12.3 and section 14
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-access with the ledger owner of rwb-decision (P7) at the contract review of RWB-P4-E8009-CON
impact: A different record code or a different set of carried fields changes the entry writer, the contract's record declaration and one test; the transaction rule and the MSG-P7-003 refusal do not change.

text: The letter template version lives in rwb-comms and this story is the approval gate and the record: rwb-access reads the version through the P6 contract, hands the approval to the P6 approve operation, records the approving role code and the time in its own decision-record chain and answers the history from that chain; it reads no template, notice or merge-field row and holds no copy of a template body, a merge field or a template state.
why: The legacy story holds the template and the notice in one schema with the decision log, and the ownership map moves all three template tables to P6 while the metadata of this story carries no P6 contract dependency; the split between the gate and the owner of the template has to be fixed on Day 1, or the story would either invent a dependency it may not add or read a foreign table it may not read.
read: Ownership Map v1 (template, notice, merge_field = P6; API POST /admin/templates and POST /admin/templates/{templateId}/approve = P6); Architecture v5 slide 41; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 and appendix T-A API-P6-003 to API-P6-007; TSD P4 v3 T6.3; FSD P4 v3 A2.21; Template and Rules R5.4 dependency class C and R5.5 DP-01
applied_in: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 6 to 16; section 8 Business rule BR5; section 11 Data; section 12.2 and 12.7 Contract; section 13 Build step 3
confirm: Solution architect and the P6 rwb-comms tech lead when the P6 template contract is published
impact: If the P6 contract renames a path or a field, or answers the read by id differently, only CommsTemplateClient, its fake and the contract test change; the gate, its two refusals and the history stay as specified. The missing C dependency is added to the metadata at D1 and no template table enters rwb_access.

text: The approving role recorded on a template approval is RW-COMPLY, the role the FSD A2.21.3.3 role table names, while the right that opens the gate is Rules and parameters A of TSD P4 v3 T6.1, which that matrix gives to RW-RISK (RA) and RW-COE (CRUD) and not to RW-COMPLY (R only); the SIT approver holds RW-COMPLY and holds the A letter, and the four-eyes rule of T6.3 holds in either reading, because the author of a version can never approve it.
why: The FSD role table and the T6.1 matrix disagree on who approves a letter template, R-PREC puts the technical specification above the functional one, and a story may not change a metadata value; without a default the recorded role code, the right that is authorised and the test data would contradict one another.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.21.3.3 roles and permissions; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 RBAC matrix; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 author and approver; legacy RWB-E8-010 permission checks (Rules and parameters C for RW-COE and A for RW-RISK); Template and Rules R3 R-PREC
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 5 and 8; section 7 Background and AC4; section 8 Business rules BR3, BR4 and BR6; section 10 Authority; section 13 Configuration and reference data
confirm: Solution architect with Compliance and the access administrator at the P4 design review
impact: If the matrix is corrected to give RW-COMPLY the A letter, or if Compliance is read to approve under the RW-RISK letter, only the role-to-letters row and the SIT test users change; the gate, the four-eyes refusal and the field that records the approving role code do not.

text: The approval history answers, for each approved version, the template version, the state APPROVED, the approving role code, the time of the approval and the approval reference, and never a name, an e-mail address or a user reference: the approver user reference that rwb-comms holds in approved_by stays with rwb-comms and is not answered by this service.
why: REQ-OCC-002 asks that the approval be recorded against the version and the template table holds the approver as a user reference (DF-REF-063), while the record of a decision may not copy personal data into its payload or its reads; a default is needed on what the history says about who approved a version.
read: TSD P6 v2 T3.1 DF-REF-063 approved_by, DF-REF-064 approved_at and DF-REF-065 valid_from; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 author and approver; REQ-OCC-002; NFR-040; the guardrails of the legacy story RWB-E8-010
applied_in: Section 1 Story; section 7 AC5; section 8 Business rules BR6, BR8, BR9 and BR10; section 11 Data; section 12.1 Contract; section 17 Guardrails
confirm: Data steward with Internal audit at the contract review
impact: If audit needs the person, the answer is a second read of the rwb-comms approval and not a field of this service's record; the history fields, the entry payload and the tests do not change.
